clue.text: Birdie making impression on golf club?

definitions.text: Birdie making impression on golf club?

parts.words: Birdie making impression on golf club?
parts.note: a birdie is a golf score, but here it is a little bird, and the golf club is a wood that it taps holes into

explanation.surface: A golfer's birdie seems to leave its mark on the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdie' and 'golf club' set a golf scene; read literally, a bird that pecks dents into wood is described.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird drills into tree trunks with its beak, so it makes impressions on timber.

clue.text: It's said to stop the drink supply

definitions.text: It's said to stop the drink supply

parts.words: It's said to stop the drink supply
parts.note: the word a guest says to tell the person pouring that the glass is full enough

explanation.surface: A ruling that halts the flow of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' reads as 'reportedly'; it is literally the word uttered at the bar or table.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pouring asks you to 'say when', and uttering the word stops the pour.

clue.text: Can this one-stone object be cut into kilos perhaps?

indicators.note: the word be is cut into the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the letters of kilos may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Could a monument be sliced up and sold by weight?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether a monument could be sold by weight; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'cut into' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering pillar carved from a single block is a monolith.

clue.text: Fishermen's prayers

parts.note: the Latin name of the Lord's Prayer is also the name of an angler's line with hooks set along it

explanation.surface: Anglers praying for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: A paternoster is both the Lord's Prayer (Our Father) and a fishing rig with hooks at intervals, like beads on a rosary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Our Father prayers share a name with sea anglers' multi-hook tackle.

clue.text: Motorist's luggage? Those beastly trunks

definitions.meaning: the bodies of dead animals, trunks belonging to beasts

explanation.surface: A driver complains about awful suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly trunks' reads as horrid luggage; it means animal bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Car cases are a driver's luggage, and carcases are the dead bodies of animals.

clue.text: One of three — press for the fourth

definitions.meaning: the three traditional orders of the realm: clergy, nobility and commons
journalism is called the fourth of these orders

explanation.surface: Lobbying for a fourth member of a trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press for' reads as 'demand'; the press is itself the fourth estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The three estates of the realm were lords spiritual, lords temporal and commons; newspapers are dubbed the fourth.

clue.text: Is better off than Simple Simon with this security device

definitions.text: Is better off than Simple Simon
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Simple Simon has no penny for the pieman, so anyone who has a P (penny) is better off
a hinged metal fastening closed with a padlock

explanation.surface: A comparison with the nursery-rhyme simpleton leads to a lock on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as HAS P: has a penny, which Simple Simon of the rhyme lacked. P is the abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate or lid fastening that slips over a staple and takes a padlock is exactly a security fitting.

clue.text: Is splitting a big volume, to make tiny pieces

indicators.note: the word Is splits the volume by going inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking a huge book apart to shred it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness, but here it is a book; 'splitting' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise is to reduce something to minute particles or fragments.

clue.text: Are such gentry bound to support Right?

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece is placed beneath the first, supporting it

parts.note: proper means right or correct
tied means bound

explanation.surface: Are landed people obliged to back the political right?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts TIED under PROPER; 'bound' looks like 'obliged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed gentry own estates, so they are land-owning people of means.

clue.text: Cross-section of the public?

parts.note: a cross-section usually means a representative sample, but here it is the part of the public that marks a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A pollster's representative sample of the population.
explanation.walkthrough: Voters mark their choice with a cross, so the voting public is the 'cross' section.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone entitled to vote, putting crosses on ballot papers, forms the body of voters.

clue.text: The lake spelled the end of Puccini

annotationWithheld.why: The lake spelled the end of Puccini (4): COMO is the lake, but no reading of 'spelled the end of Puccini' gives or supports COMO (Puccini died in Brussels and lived by Lake Massaciuccoli)
annotationWithheld.clue: The lake spelled the end of Puccini

clue.text: 9 includes many in county set, perhaps

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be rearranged

explanation.surface: Voters include many county-set people.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is ELECTORATE. 'perhaps' scrambles C, IN and COUNTY SET; 'county set' suggests upper-class country society.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters of one parliamentary seat make up the seat's body of electors.

clue.text: Support essential for bridge contract?

definitions.meaning: a pillar or column that holds something up
any firm contracted to build a span over a river needs these masonry columns to carry it

explanation.surface: A bridge player wonders what backing a contract needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge contract' sounds like the card game, where a contract is a bid; here it is a construction job.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge spans rest on these masonry columns, which are the uprights that bear their weight.

clue.text: Sanction anagram from all the vowels and consonants in short

indicators.note: the clue openly says the following letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: the five vowels A, E, I, O, U
the consonants of the word short are S, H, R, T

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter approves a word game built from letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' plainly asks for the rearrangement of AEIOU plus SHRT; 'short' looks like 'in brief' but is the source word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction an action is to permit it officially, giving it approval.

clue.text: With no change at all in the place, fills up money-drawer

definitions.text: With no change at all in the place

parts.note: stocks means fills up, as a shop does its shelves
a till is a shop's cash drawer

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper restocks and loads the cash register without moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no change' suggests no coins in the till; it means not moving at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means utterly motionless, staying put without any movement.

clue.text: Deal, when director demands a cut.

definitions.meaning: a business deal in which one company buys control of another
a film director shouting cut and calling for the scene to be shot again

explanation.surface: A business deal where the boss insists on a share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' and 'cut' read as a company director wanting a slice; in film a director's cut stops a take, which is then done over.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyout is a deal transferring control of a firm; a scene reshot is done once more, a take again.

clue.text: .a risky proposition- Times leader's view

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a risky venture

indicators.note: a leader is the head of something, so the first letter of Times is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial calls something a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from 15; 'Times leader' suggests a newspaper editorial but just gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A view of a matter is one angle or facet from which it is seen.

clue.text: Auburn deserter ?

parts.note: Auburn is the village of Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village, so one who left it is a resident who went

explanation.surface: A red-haired runaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auburn' looks like a hair colour; Goldsmith's poem opens 'Sweet Auburn, loveliest village of the plain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deserting Goldsmith's abandoned settlement would be one of its inhabitants.

clue.text: The main rising he could not check

definitions.text: The main rising he could not check

parts.words: The main rising he could not check
parts.note: the main is the sea and its rising is the incoming tide, which a legendary king ordered back in vain

explanation.surface: A ruler fails to stop a principal revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main rising' reads as a chief uprising; 'the main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish-English king of legend sat on the shore and commanded the tide to halt, proving it obeyed no monarch.

clue.text: It's clear Labour TV set-up

parts.note: to clear a sum after deductions is to net it
labour means work

explanation.surface: A comment that the Labour Party is clearly behind a television arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with a capital suggests the political party; it is just toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting network is the system of linked stations running television.

clue.text: Fine work of reformed girl I put in charge

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: the letters of girl and I are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward girl, now reformed, is given responsibility for delicate work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in charge' sounds like promotion of the reformed girl, but it places the rearranged letters (ILIGR) inside the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental wirework, a very fine piece of craft.

clue.text: disturbs Tories-right to create uproar

indicators.note: disturbing the letters of Tories throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: Something unsettles the Conservatives, and the right wing causes a rumpus.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from 19; 'disturbs' signals the rearrangement of the party name, with R added after.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily and boisterously.

clue.text: Cause fire damage to HQ of Scottish orthodox churches ?

parts.note: Sc is the abbreviation for Scottish
or here is the first two letters of orthodox
ch is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Arsonists threaten the headquarters of Scotland's traditional churches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HQ of' asks for the head of each word, taken two letters at a time: SC, OR, CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch something is to burn its surface, harming it with heat.

clue.text: Making fun of/racialist organization

indicators.note: organizing the letters of racialist puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A clue for mocking a racist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' looks like a group of racists; it signals reorganizing the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire mocks its target, so a satirical piece is ridiculing someone.

clue.text: Communities want this group to become Reds

indicators.note: to want is to lack, so the word Communities lacks this answer's letters and what remains spells another word

parts.note: the four letters sit together inside Communities, but not as a hidden word: the clue's mechanism is removing them so that Reds is left, and the hidden run is a coincidence of that removal
Commies is slang for communists, Reds

explanation.surface: Left-wing communities aim to turn a group communist.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the answer out of COMMUNITIES and COMMIES (Reds) remains: 'want' means 'lack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single group forming part of a larger body, like an army unit.

clue.text: About to enter 26 (it's open)

indicators.note: the word for about goes into the other piece

parts.note: 26 across is IRON, whose chemical symbol is Fe
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A note that a metal door is unlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is IRON, chemical symbol FE; RE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean open, as in unobstructed or available to all.

clue.text: —, Cold—, is master of them all" (Kipling)

definitions.text: —, Cold—, is master of them all" (Kipling)

parts.words: —, Cold—, is master of them all" (Kipling)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Kipling's poem Cold ..., in which this metal beats gold, silver and copper

explanation.surface: A gap-filling line from Kipling's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem runs 'Gold is for the mistress, silver for the maid...', ending with the metal of the sword ruling all; the same word fills both blanks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's poem the metal of swords and weapons rules over all the precious ones.

clue.text: One who raised the issue with his partner

definitions.text: One who raised the issue with his partner

parts.words: One who raised the issue with his partner
parts.note: raising an issue sounds like bringing up a topic, but issue means offspring, raised by a parent with a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone brought up a matter jointly with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' in law means children, and raising it means bringing them up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor or forefather begets children with a mate and so starts a line of descent.

clue.text: Not-so-hot gospeller?

definitions.meaning: a writer of one of the four Gospels, the evangelist who was a physician

explanation.surface: A preacher who lacks fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the start of LUKEWARM, tepid, and also the third evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke- in lukewarm means tepid; Saint Luke wrote the third Gospel.

clue.text: Red actor with part in Chekhov play

parts.note: cherry is a bright red colour
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A left-wing actor has a role in a Russian drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red actor' suggests a communist performer; TREE is the actor-manager Beerbohm Tree. The play is The Cherry Orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard is about an orchard of such fruit trees, so each one is part of it.
